title: What syncopation means in reading
summary: Hall defines syncopation as dividing notes when reading and talks about studio readers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Sure. As far as syncopation is concerned, could you tell me what you mean when you say the syncopation?
Syncopation is the main thing about reading music.
I mean like you know how to divide your notes, divide the passages, you know.
You mean like a fast note, a longer note?

Yeah, well the way they write, your eighth note, your sixteenth note, you know how to divide them. Sometimes your notes will tie it over to another one, you know how to divide them up. It's the same as figuring out something. Well you get guys like playing in the studio, do that every day, it comes just like anything. They look at a sheet and a lot of them can tell whether they can read it or not. Of course some, they've got to have rehearsed like anything. You get used to that, but when you get away from it, then you've got to get back, you know, work into it. You know what I mean? Sure. You get some guys can transport four and five notes apart, four and five tones apart.
